findings.reason: The protected SQL implementation uses ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) inside a CTE to rank each customer's orders by recency, joins to Customers, filters recency_rank <= 3, and orders the output by customer_name ASC, customer_id ASC, order_date DESC. The solution is canonical, optimal, and concise; no candidate is required.

Because each customer places at most one order per date, ROW_NUMBER() produces an unambiguous recency rank without ties. Filtering recency_rank <= 3 keeps at most the three newest orders for each customer. Customers with fewer than 3 orders retain all their orders, and customers with zero orders produce no rows.

Window-function ranking and final multi-key ordering take O(m log m) time across m orders, and joining to c customers takes O(c + m) time. Working space is O(c + m). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.

Projects customer_name, customer_id, order_id, and order_date in the required column format and applies the multi-column sort (customer_name ASC, customer_id ASC, order_date DESC) specified by the contract.

The approach accurately details windowed ranking by customer_id, filtering for ranks 1 to 3, joining customer details, and enforcing the 3-part presentation sort. Alternatives and edge cases cover correlated subqueries, session variables, fewer than 3 orders, tie-breaking by customer_id, and unique daily order guarantees.
